items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: 'Toe' Morgan had a job on Christmas Day, 1924. He said, 'Hayes, come on and play this job with us.'

ctx.x: So, I said, well, I don't need a guy like him to be teaching me, you know what I mean, if he was going to try to rob me out of my brand new horn -- and my horn wasn't even paid for -- quite paid for. Do you know what I mean?

So, I went on back and went back to the woodshed, as we called it. Went back to the woodshed and kept on practicing, kept on practicing. So, I got so I could play a few tunes. And the first tune I really learned as 'You can see your momma every night. Can't see your poppa at all (singing).' So, there was a fellow, a drummer named James Morgan -- his nickname was 'Toe' Morgan. 'Toe' Morgan had a job on Christmas Day, 1924. He said, 'Hayes, come on and play this job with us.' I said, 'Toe', I'm not good enough to…
